args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted when the release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is passing health checks again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 is the newest release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. us-east, us-west and eu-west now all run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. No approval was needed, since the approval policy only covers deploying versions that have never been healthy in production.
- **Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api):** It covers the failure, the rollback and the current state. It also lists two follow-ups: finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and finding out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed health checks in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
